Learn 冴 through 冴える (さえる): to be clear-headed or alert, or vivid and clear in appearance or sound. The verb can also describe deft performance. An older sense concerns intense cold; coldness is not implied whenever someone is clear-headed.

冴える さえる — be clear-headed; be vivid
頭が冴える (あたまがさえる) — be clear-headed
目が冴える (めがさえる) — be wide awake; be unable to sleep

目が冴える concerns wakefulness, not eyes visibly shining. 冴えない (さえない) can describe something lacklustre, disappointing or unappealing; it is not always a literal absence of visual clarity or a judgement about intelligence.

Compare the two left-hand marks with 次, whose right side is different. 汗 and 河 have three left-hand water dots, 氵, rather than 冫. The grade-9 source classification concerns name-use kanji, but 冴える is not a name-only word. Personal-name readings are outside this card's scope.

冴える さえる — be clear-headed; be vivid

冴える describes mental clarity or alertness, and a crisp, vivid quality in sights, colours or sounds. Learn the whole expression with its subject: 頭が冴える (あたまがさえる) means to be clear-headed; 目が冴える (めがさえる) means to be wide awake, often when you would rather sleep.
今日は頭が冴えています。 (きょうはあたまがさえています。) — I feel clear-headed today.
目が冴えて眠れません。 (めがさえてねむれません。) — I'm wide awake and can't sleep.

This is an intransitive ichidan verb: the subject takes が. Forms include 冴えます (さえます), 冴えた (さえた), 冴えて (さえて) and 冴えない (さえない). 冴えている can describe an existing alert state. The examples adapt dictionary examples to polite endings.

冴 supplies the clarity meaning in this single-kanji native verb. In the written form 冴える, 冴 represents さ and the following える completes さえる. The conjugation stem is さえ, including the written え. It is not a compound assembled from on readings.
JMdict also records 冱える (さえる) as a rarely used kanji spelling. That spelling flag does not make the pronunciation さえる rare.

覚める (さめる) focuses on waking or regaining awareness: 目が覚める (めがさめる) means "wake up," whereas 目が冴える describes wakefulness. 澄む (すむ) and 透き通る (すきとおる) overlap for clear sound, but physical transparency is not a universal meaning of 冴える.
For an opposite evaluation, 冴えない can mean "lacklustre" or "unsatisfactory," depending on what is being described; it is not a single antonym for every sense.

冴える can describe deft technique or a well-executed performance, not only mental alertness. It does not generally mean a permanent high intelligence score, nor does 目が冴える mean eyes lighting up with happiness.

The negative 冴えない often concerns a disappointing result, an unappealing appearance or a subdued condition rather than literal blur. An older, somewhat old-fashioned sense of 冴える is "become intensely cold." For ordinary cooling, learn 冷える (ひえる); for freezing, 凍る (こおる). Those verbs are not alternative pronunciations of the 冴える taught here.
